name: A 2029-Concept Attachment Showing the Punctured-Square Test Is Strictly Weaker
definition: Take the 1165-concept binary block replacement of the established 581-concept edge piece. It retains a specified punctured root square but does not retain the full root square. Attach the archived 289-concept rooted factor along that punctured square.
parameters: The block has 1165 concepts. The attached family has 2029 concepts in dimension 26.
properties: A complete corner order peels the attachment: first use the archived relative order to the punctured square, then lift the rooted-factor order in its three retained fibres. The first piece fails to retain the full square by the existing full-fibre reduction to its root-negative 289-concept class. Thus punctured-square retention is locally strictly weaker than full-square retention.
